doc.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021

title: Hearing the New York scene in the first six months of college
summary: He lists the concerts he heard after arriving in 1971, including Konitz, Elvin Jones, Thad Jones-Mel Lewis, Return to Forever, Mingus and Rollins, plus free shows at the New York Jazz Museum.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: In the years, let’s say the early 70s, I think you had returned to New York.
I went for the first time. I went to college in New York from ’71 to ’75.
Okay. Did you go to clubs as often as you could afford let’s say, and do you recall hearing any particular group or individual that just sort of blew you away?

Everything man. I mean look I arrived in New York in the fall of 1971 and in the first six months I was in New York I can tell you who I heard. And you have to remember that I went to clubs as much as I could on my limited college kid’s budget. But there was also a lot of free stuff going on, free meaning no charge. But the first six months I heard Lee Konitz playing with a minimalist named Lamont Young in the Metropolitan Museum actually; then I heard Elvin Jones’ quartet in a little auditorium on the upper west side © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

with Joe Farrell and Dave Liebman and Gene Perla; I heard the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band at the Village Vanguard, this was the first of a number of times I heard them at the Vanguard; I heard Chick Corea and Return to Forever, their first gig at the Village Vanguard, this was the Return to Forever with Joe Farrell and Flora Purim and Stanley Clarke, and I heard Airto Moreira, this was their first gig ever and it was one of the greatest nights of live music I have ever heard, as good as the records were that they made. In person they were just stunning. I heard Charles Mingus’ all-star big band at Philharmonic Hall with Lee Konitz, Gerry Mulligan, Gene Ammons, Milt Hinton, Joe Chambers, Jon Faddis. I heard Sonny Rollins at the Vanguard with Albert Dailey, Larry Ridley and David Lee. This was the first six months you know. And then after that well I was in school. There was a lot of, as I said, there were a lot of free concerts going on. There was this place on 55th Street called the New York Jazz Museum that opened up while I was in college. They would have Sunday afternoon concerts for free. And I heard a bunch of people there. I heard Howard McGhee and Joe Carroll. I heard Hank Mobley. I heard Thad and Mel with the quintet with Billy Harper and George Mraz and Walter Norris. Jimmy Guiffre. You know this was all for free you know. You could just go on a Sunday afternoon.
